claims.text: The relevant Al_xCoCrCuFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy is multiphase.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature generate debris from the alloy surface.
Corrosion-modified debris acts as a third-body abrasive within the wear interface.
Repeated entry of corrosion-modified debris into the wear interface intensifies mechanical abrasion.
Third-body abrasion accelerates the breakdown or removal of protective surface layers.
Enhanced abrasion continuously exposes fresh alloy surfaces.
Exposure of fresh alloy surfaces promotes additional localized corrosion.
The interaction between abrasive debris, fresh-surface exposure, and corrosion forms a positive feedback loop.
The positive feedback loop causes combined degradation to exceed the sum of separately measured wear and corrosion contributions.
A closed debris-retention configuration will accumulate more wear-corrosion debris than an actively flushed configuration.
Debris retention will produce greater total degradation than debris removal under otherwise matched conditions.
Debris retention will produce greater wear-volume loss than debris removal.
Debris retention will produce a higher density of corrosion pits than debris removal.
Debris retention will produce deeper corrosion pits than debris removal.
With debris removal, simultaneous wear and corrosion will be approximately additive because third-body amplification is absent.
Changing conditions outside approximately 650 °C, a chloride-rich electrolyte, and the standardized wear load may activate additional degradation mechanisms.

contradictions.description: The setups are said to differ only in debris management, but lubrication is offered as an alternative debris-removal method. Lubrication also changes friction, contact mechanics, heat generation, and potentially corrosion chemistry, so it is not an otherwise identical comparison.

The debris-removal configuration is defined as the baseline simultaneous wear-corrosion test, yet the predicted outcome refers to isolated wear and isolated corrosion contributions as being observed in baseline conditions. Those isolated contributions require additional wear-only and corrosion-only controls and are not supplied by the stated baseline.
